title: Mosconi Cup 2026 Day 1 Results: USA and Europe Level 2-2 After Opening Night
description: Mosconi Cup 2026 Day 1 results from Orlando: USA won a hill-hill Teams Match, Europe hit back twice, and Van Boening and Styer leveled it 2-2. Every match, the key racks and what's next.
body:
After four matches on opening night at the Caribe Royale Resort in Orlando, the 2026 Mosconi Cup is all square: USA 2, Europe 2. Team USA won a nervy Teams Match on the final rack. Europe answered with two straight wins, then Shane Van Boening and Tyler Styer put on the best doubles display of the night to pull the home side level. Both teams are nine points away from the 11 needed to win the Cup.

Mosconi Cup 2026 Day 1: every result

MatchResultOverall
1. Teams MatchUSA 5-4 EuropeUSA 1-0
2. DoublesFrancisco Sánchez Ruiz & Joshua Filler (EUR) 5-2 Fedor Gorst & Justin Bergman (USA)1-1
3. SinglesAleksa Pecelj (EUR) 5-2 Skyler Woodward (USA)Europe 2-1
4. DoublesShane Van Boening & Tyler Styer (USA) 5-1 Jayson Shaw & David Alcaide (EUR)2-2

Match 1: USA steal the Teams Match on the hill

Europe looked like they would run away with it. Filler won the lag, Europe took the opening rack, and Pecelj rolled in a 4-9 combination for 2-0. When Europe made it 3-0, the American crowd went quiet.

Then USA won three racks in a row to level at 3-3. Europe got to the hill first at 4-3, but Pecelj missed a long pot on the 3-ball and USA took the rack to force a hill-hill decider. In the last rack Europe had a runout in front of them, but Shaw's position on the 7-ball left Filler no choice but to play safe. The safety came up short, the 7 was left on, and USA cleared the table to win 5-4 and take the first point of the Cup.

"It's crucial to get that first match win and to have the crowd behind us," USA captain Johan Ruijsink said.

Match 2: Filler's combinations level it for Europe

Reigning US Open champion Francisco Sánchez Ruiz and six-time Cup winner Joshua Filler answered straight away against Fedor Gorst and Justin Bergman. The racks traded early. Bergman made a three-ball combination for USA, and it was 2-2 after four.

Filler then took over. After a tense safety battle he spotted a 2-9 combination for 3-2. In the next rack the 9-ball sat on the lip of the pocket, and Filler cashed a 4-9 combination to reach the hill. The Europeans broke and ran the last rack to win 5-2 and level the overall score at 1-1.

"We needed that point to level the score after the Teams Match," Filler said.

Match 3: debutant Pecelj beats Skyler Woodward

The first singles match of the week was a big test for Aleksa Pecelj, playing his first Mosconi Cup, against two-time MVP Skyler Woodward. Woodward drew first blood with a smart safety on the 2-ball. Two Woodward scratches, the first after a push-out, then gave Pecelj two racks and a 2-1 lead. A dry break from Pecelj let Woodward back in at 2-2, but the Serbian won the last three racks to win 5-2 and put Europe in front.

"Bring them all, one by one. I'm ready for it," Pecelj said afterward.

Match 4: Van Boening and Styer pull USA level

In his record 20th straight Mosconi Cup, Shane Van Boening played like he had something to prove. He and Tyler Styer faced Jayson Shaw and David Alcaide, the same matchup as last year's doubles that sealed Europe's sixth straight title.

Styer kicked out of an Alcaide safety on the 2-ball to set up the opening rack. Europe leveled after a Van Boening safety missed its mark, but after that it was all USA. Styer and Shaw both missed the 9-ball in the third rack before USA got it down for 2-1. A dry break from Shaw and a loose Alcaide safety put the Americans on the hill at 4-1, and when Alcaide scratched on the break, Van Boening and Styer ran out to win 5-1.

"I've never seen him play as well in the Mosconi Cup. That's the best he's ever played," Styer said of his partner.

Day 1 takeaways

  • USA can win the close ones. Taking the Teams Match from 0-3 down and then hill-hill is the kind of rack Europe usually wins. It gave the home crowd something to roar about.
  • Filler is Filler. Two clutch combinations turned a level doubles match into a comfortable win.
  • Pecelj is not fazed. The Mosconi Cup rookie beat one of the USA's most dangerous singles players in his first match.
  • Van Boening looks sharp. If Shane plays like this all weekend, Europe's run of six straight titles is in real danger.

What's next: Day 2 on Saturday, November 28

Play resumes Saturday at 1:00 PM ET (10:00 AM PT) at the Caribe Royale, live on ESPN+ in the US and WNT TV everywhere else. The race is to 11 points, so there is a long way to go. USA will be looking for its first lead of the week, and Europe for its seventh straight title.
